sources.title: Project seed pronunciation choices through v0.9
sources.note: Authored project policies; no external pronunciation authority or human approval is asserted.

sources.title: PostgreSQL Press FAQ: pronunciation
sources.note: Official English pronunciation guide post-GRES-que-ell; Korean transcription is an editorial inference, not attested here.

sources.title: Project general lexical/numeric pattern policy v0.20
sources.note: Developer-authored provisional pronunciation policy for top + number composition. No external source or independent human pronunciation approval is asserted.

sources.title: Project email/URL word reading policy v0.21
sources.note: Developer-authored provisional Korean readings for common mail/portal host labels and the reserved example domain. No external source or independent human pronunciation approval is asserted.

sources.title: Project acronym word-readings authored for v0.21
sources.note: Standard Korean loanword spellings for acronyms that Korean reads as words, authored by the project after the runtime spelled them letter by letter. No external pronunciation authority, no human approval and no synthesized audio.

sources.title: Project Korean readings for bare unit abbreviations, v0.21
sources.note: Standard Korean unit names for abbreviations that appear without a number. No external pronunciation authority, no human approval and no synthesized audio.

sources.title: Apparel size readings in the AI Hub 159 Korean references
sources.note: Counts of how the provided Korean references read bare and multiplied apparel sizes (XL 엑스라지 41:2, XS 엑스스몰 8:5). Reference agreement, not linguistic approval; no synthesized audio.

sources.title: Unit and technology-term readings in the AI Hub 159 Korean references
sources.note: Counts of how the provided references read 5G, 4K, gold purity and unit variants. Reference agreement, not linguistic approval; no synthesized audio.

sources.title: Project-owner reading decisions of 2026-10-01 (3M, unit control)
sources.note: The company name 3M is read 쓰리엠 and a meter reading is requested with 3M{@unit}. Project decision, not independent linguistic approval; no synthesized audio.

sources.title: Project readings of common English words in Korean context, v24
sources.note: Authored by the project from the 외래어 표기법 English rules and established usage. Words were chosen by frequency in local Korean-context text whose spelling guess was wrong; no reading is copied from a corpus.

sources.title: Project acronym word-readings, v24 (표준국어대사전 survey)
sources.note: Acronyms the 표준국어대사전 lists as loanwords read as words, kept by hand only when still read that way in current Korean. The dictionary (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) is confirming evidence; the readings are the common Korean ones. No human approval and no synthesized audio.

sources.title: Project readings of foreign proper nouns, v24
sources.note: Foreign proper nouns whose spelling guess is wrong in Korean-context text, read with their established Korean spelling (외래어 표기법 and common usage). No human approval and no synthesized audio.

sources.title: Project readings of English day, month and given names in Korean context, v25
sources.note: English day and month names and common given names whose spelling guess was wrong in a mixed Korean/English text (Friday 프리데이, John 조흔), read with the 외래어 표기법 spelling or established usage. No human approval and no synthesized audio.

sources.title: Project readings of common English words in Korean context, v26
sources.note: Common English words whose spelling guess was wrong in a mixed Korean/English text (English 엥리시, Set 셋, Tech 텍, regex 리겍스), read with the 외래어 표기법 spelling or established usage; regex 레젝스 by the project owner. No human approval and no synthesized audio.

sources.title: Project readings of accented words in Korean context, v27
sources.note: Common brand, name and food words written with accents (Pokémon, Beyoncé, jalapeño) that the 표준국어대사전 loanword table does not have, read with their established Korean spelling (외래어 표기법 and common usage). Keys are the spelling without accents, as the engine looks them up. No human approval is claimed.

sources.title: Project readings of English names, brands and capital words in Korean context, v28
sources.note: Common names, brands, capital acronym-words and signage words whose reading was wrong in Korean speech (ZARA 지에이알에이, Nike 나이크, Johnson 조흐느슨, Christmas 크리스트매스), read with the 외래어 표기법 spelling or established Korean usage. Project-owner request 2026-10-28. No human approval and no synthesized audio.

sources.title: Project readings of music names, title words and contractions in Korean context, v29
sources.note: Artist names, English song-title words, music terms and contractions whose reading was wrong in Korean speech (BLACKPINK spelled out, aespa 애에스파, Supernova 서퍼노바, Don't 던티), read with established Korean usage in music news and broadcasting. Project-owner request 2026-10-29. No human approval and no synthesized audio.

sources.title: Project readings found by the TN improvement rounds in Korean context, v30
sources.note: Artist names, song-title words, brands and key names whose reading was wrong in the round evaluation sets (Peaches 피처즈, KakaoTalk 캐캐오토크, Ctrl 씨티알엘), read with the 외래어 표기법 spelling or established Korean usage. TN improvement rounds 2026-10-29. No human approval and no synthesized audio.

sources.title: Project readings of Korean ETF brands and listed company names, v31
sources.note: ETF brands and listed company names whose reading was wrong in a stock-name test of 1,929 non-Hangul names (ACE 에이씨이, SOL 에스오엘, HANARO 해나로, WON 더블유오엔, KoAct 코크트), read as the brands are pronounced. Project-owner request 2026-11-02 (TN round 35). No human approval and no synthesized audio.
